e: Posterior cricoarytenoid is the sole abductor (opener) of the vocal cords — all other laryngeal muscles adduct/tense.
SSNHL mainstay = urgent systemic corticosteroids, c̅ intratympanic steroids reserved as salvage.
Melkersson-Rosenthal triad = recurrent LMN facial palsy + orofacial granulomatous oedema + fissured tongue; proptosis is not part of it.
Cochlear base (high frequencies) degenerates first – presbycusis c̅ high-pitch loss.
Glottic T stage depends on cord mobility, commissure involvement and spread to paraglottic space/thyroid cartilage.
PTA needs voluntary response – not possible in infants (OAE, BERA used).
FESS sequence: uncinectomy → maxillary antrostomy → bullectomy → ethmoidectomy.
Piriform fossa mucosa is supplied by the internal branch of superior laryngeal n. (sensory).
Otitis media complication c̅ fever and neck stiffness → otogenic meningitis.
JNA: biopsy is contraindicated (profuse bleeding); diagnosis is by CT/MRI c̅ angiography.
Brief positional vertigo c̅ no hearing loss → BPPV (Dix-Hallpike +ve, Epley manoeuvre).
Cochlear implant is for profound SNHL (congenital, post-ototoxic); otosclerosis/ossicular fixation are conductive (stapedectomy/hearing aid).
Laryngomalacia (commonest) and subglottic stenosis cause stridor in infants.
